clue.text: Worker is about to live here, in France

parts.note: a worker is an ant, the classic toiling insect of the colony

indicators.note: about means the first piece goes round the second here, wrapping it

parts.note: to live is to be, simply to exist

explanation.surface: A labourer is on the point of settling down somewhere in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'here, in France' defines a place: the resort on the Riviera, the French Mediterranean coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Antibes is a resort town on the French Riviera, so it is a place located in France.

clue.text: Chief adversary's out of reach

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown out of their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Your worst enemy is safely beyond your grasp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the seven letters of OF REACH; the 's is a link meaning 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An arch-foe is a principal enemy, arch- meaning foremost, so a chief adversary.

clue.text: Informed about a tree's destruction, suffered

indicators.note: about means the first word goes around the other letters

parts.note: informed means told, as in 'told the police'

indicators.note: destruction suggests the letters of the words are broken up and remade

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Someone told of the felling of a tree put up with it.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive 's adds no letter: only the five letters of 'a tree' are scrambled before going inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To tolerate something is to endure or put up with it, so tolerated matches suffered.

clue.text: Using trasnsport system, set off for this place

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the former national railway network of the UK

indicators.note: off suggests the letters are set going in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A traveller takes the railway and sets out for a destination.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges SET into EST. British Rail ran the UK's railways until the 1990s. 'trasnsport' is a misprint in the source for 'transport'.
explanation.definitionFit: Brest is a port city in Brittany, the place the clue points to.

clue.text: Girl is uplifted, finding natural earth

indicators.note: uplifted in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young woman is cheered up by discovering some unspoilt soil.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'uplifted' reads both pieces upwards as one run.
explanation.definitionFit: Sienna is a natural pigment, an earth containing iron oxide used to colour paint.

clue.text: Declining in morals, Carol chases after retreating chum

indicators.note: chases after places one piece following the other
retreating means the word goes backwards

parts.note: a chum is a pal, a friend
to carol is to sing

explanation.surface: A carol singer runs after a friend who backs away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a girl's name but is the verb; 'chases after' places the second piece behind the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Lapsing describes falling away from a standard of behaviour, sliding morally.

clue.text: Apprentice has to move with slow caution to secure vital part

parts.note: L is a learner, as on British L-plates for learner drivers
to inch is to move forward slowly and carefully
to pin something is to fasten it securely

explanation.surface: A trainee edges carefully forward to fix a key component in place.
explanation.definitionFit: A linchpin is the essential element that holds everything together, a crucial component.

clue.text: Left sheet of paper in case

parts.note: port is the nautical term for the left side of a ship
a folio is a sheet of paper, folded once

explanation.surface: Someone has left a page inside a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A portfolio is a flat carrying case for papers or drawings.

clue.text: Harden in the river

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: Something is toughened by being plunged into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a North Yorkshire river, a crossword regular.
explanation.definitionFit: To inure is to accustom someone to hardship, toughening them against it.

clue.text: Argue heatedly with Scottish banker, there's a bit missing from the payment

indicators.note: heatedly suggests the letters are stirred up into a new order
missing means the named piece is taken away from the word

parts.note: a bit here is just the letter A, a little piece of the word
a banker is a river (it has banks); the Don flows through Aberdeen in Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone disputes angrily with a Scottish bank because their money falls short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' drops A from ARGUE, and 'heatedly' scrambles the rest to GUER. 'banker' meaning river is a crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Guerdon is an archaic word for a reward or recompense.

clue.text: Where we may learn old king is detaining member

indicators.note: is detaining means the first word holds the other inside it

parts.note: Old King Cole is the merry monarch of the nursery rhyme
a leg is a limb, a member of the body

explanation.surface: An ancient ruler is holding a club member in custody.
explanation.definitionFit: A college is an institution of higher education, a place of study.

clue.text: Give direction to straying uturner

indicators.note: straying suggests the letters wander out of place into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone tries to set a wayward U-turning driver on the right path.
explanation.definitionFit: To nurture is to bring up and guide, giving direction as a parent would.

clue.text: Initial placing of trees in meadow? About time!

indicators.note: about means the other pieces go around the letter for time

parts.note: firs are coniferous trees
in a meadow is in the field

explanation.surface: Planting trees in a field first is overdue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' puts T inside FIRS IN THE FIELD, just after FIRS.
explanation.definitionFit: Being first in the field is the earliest position, ahead of rivals, so an initial placing.

clue.text: Involve in late redeployment

indicators.note: redeployment suggests the letters are moved around to new positions

explanation.surface: Someone is drawn into a last-minute reorganisation of staff.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail is to necessitate or involve as a consequence.

clue.text: Amount added in building material with right ingredient

indicators.note: ingredient means the letter is mixed in as a part of the larger word

parts.note: cement is a building material

explanation.surface: Extra is put into the mortar, with the correct component.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ingredient' makes the letter for right a component mixed into the building material.
explanation.definitionFit: An increment is an increase, a quantity added on.

clue.text: Young William may be of use to campers

parts.note: Billy is a familiar form of William, used for a boy
may means can, as in 'you may go'

explanation.surface: A boy called William might be helpful on a camping trip.
explanation.definitionFit: A billycan is a metal cooking pot used over a campfire, a camping utensil.

clue.text: Grave entry -— imprisonment!

definitions.meaning: the placing of a body in a grave, a burial
the sending of someone to prison or an institution

explanation.definitionFit: Committal is both the burial part of a funeral service and the act of consigning someone to prison.

clue.text: No treaty? This lawman is at fault

indicators.note: at fault suggests the letters are wrong and must be put right

explanation.surface: With no agreement signed, the lawyer is to blame.
explanation.definitionFit: An attorney is a lawyer, especially in the US, so a man of the law.

clue.text: A duty CIA carried out called for nerve

indicators.note: carried out suggests the letters are taken out and laid down again differently

explanation.surface: A mission performed by American intelligence required courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Audacity is boldness or cheek, the same as having the nerve.

clue.text: Separated equally, below

parts.note: as means equally, as in 'as tall as'
under means below

explanation.surface: Things are split evenly, one beneath the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Asunder means apart or into pieces, as when something is split.

clue.text: Old-fashioned chap's jacket

indicators.note: fashioned means the letters are shaped into a new form

parts.note: a chap is a man; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: A fellow owns an outdated coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashioned' turns OLD into DOL, so 'Old-fashioned' is not one word's sense here.
explanation.definitionFit: A dolman is a hussar's jacket worn over the shoulder, or a loose cloak.

clue.text: Draw a drink up for him — but don't expect him to reciprocate!

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to drag is to draw or pull
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: Someone pours a man a drink but knows he'll never buy a round back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads DRAG GIN backwards as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A niggard is a mean, stingy person who never returns generosity.

clue.text: The wake is by a grave

parts.note: stern means grave, serious

explanation.surface: A funeral vigil takes place beside a burial plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wake' and 'grave' suggest a funeral, but the wake is the trail of water behind a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern means behind a vessel, where its trail in the water lies.

clue.text: Prune viciously having found it's ugly

indicators.note: viciously suggests the letters are savaged and rearranged

parts.note: having means possessing, owning

explanation.surface: Someone finds a cruelly cut-back shrub unattractive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'viciously' rearranges PRUNE into UNPRE; 'found it's' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Unprepossessing means unattractive, failing to make a good impression.

clue.text: One associates it with Western pursuits

definitions.text: One associates it with Western pursuits

parts.words: One associates it with Western pursuits
parts.note: the surface suggests something linked in the mind with cowboy films; cryptically it is a group of associates pursuing outlaws in Westerns

explanation.definitionFit: A posse is a band of men summoned by a sheriff to chase criminals, a staple of cowboy films.

clue.text: Flare of temper is just part of the act

definitions.meaning: an emotional outburst, a public row
a subdivision of an act in a play

explanation.definitionFit: A scene is both a display of anger in public and a section within an act of a play.

clue.text: See something when riddling cinders

indicators.note: riddling means sifting, as with a riddle or sieve, so the letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone spots something while sieving the ashes.
explanation.definitionFit: To discern is to perceive or make out, to see.

clue.text: Play with treacle duff

indicators.note: duff means bad or broken, so the letters are faulty and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone toys with a failed batch of syrup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duff' looks like the pudding (plum duff), which suits treacle, but here it is British slang for useless.
explanation.definitionFit: Electra is a Greek tragedy by Sophocles, also by Euripides, so a play.

clue.text: Troops in French attempt to get access again

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
en is French for in
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Soldiers make a French assault to break back in.
explanation.definitionFit: Re-entry is the act of going in a second time, gaining access again.

clue.text: Goaded, poverty having shown the way

parts.note: need means poverty, want
led means guided, showed the way

explanation.surface: Poor people, having been guided, were spurred on.
explanation.definitionFit: Needled means provoked or irritated, like being goaded.
